paragraphs: ChoiceOne Financial Services, Inc. (the "Company") is a financial holding company registered under the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, as amended ("BHC Act"). The Company was incorporated on February 24, 1986, as a Michigan corporation. The Company was formed to create a bank holding company for the purpose of acquiring all of the capital stock of ChoiceOne Bank, which became a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company on April 6, 1987. Effective November 1, 2006, Valley Ridge Financial Corp., a one-bank holding company for Valley Ridge Bank ("VRB"), merged with and into the Company. In December 2006, VRB was consolidated into ChoiceOne Bank. Effective October 1, 2019, County Bank Corp. ("County"), a one-bank holding company for Lakestone Bank & Trust ("Lakestone"), merged with and into the Company. Lakestone was consolidated into ChoiceOne Bank in May 2020. On July 1, 2020, Community Shores Bank Corporation ("Community Shores"), a one bank holding company for Community Shores Bank, merged with and into the Company. Community Shores Bank was consolidated into ChoiceOne Bank in October 2020. ChoiceOne Bank owns all of the outstanding common stock of ChoiceOne Insurance Agencies, Inc., an independent insurance agency headquartered in Sparta, Michigan (the "Insurance Agency"). On July 18, 2023, the Company organized 109 Technologies, LLC as a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company with the intent to own intellectual property for a fintech product licensed to third party banks and bank holding companies. On March 1, 2025, the Company completed the merger (the "Merger") of Fentura Financial, Inc. ("Fentura"), the former parent company of The State Bank, with and into the Company with the Company surviving the merger. On March 14, 2025, ChoiceOne Bank completed the consolidation of The State Bank with and into ChoiceOne Bank with ChoiceOne Bank surviving the consolidation.

The Company's business is primarily concentrated in a single industry segment, banking. ChoiceOne Bank (referred to as the "Bank") is a full-service banking institution that offers a variety of deposit, payment, credit and other financial services to all types of customers. These services include time, savings, and demand deposits, safe deposit services, and automated transaction machine services. Loans, both commercial and consumer, are extended primarily on a secured basis to commercial enterprises and individuals. Commercial lending covers such categories as business, industry, agricultural, construction, inventory, and real estate. The Bank's consumer loan departments make direct and indirect loans to consumers and purchasers of residential and real property. In addition, the Bank offers trust and wealth management services. No material part of the business of the Company or the Bank is dependent upon a single customer or very few customers, the loss of which would have a materially adverse effect on the Company.

The Bank's primary market areas lie within western, central, and southeastern Michigan, in the communities where the Bank's respective offices are located. The Bank serves these markets through 47 full-service offices, one drive up office, five loan production offices and a wealth management office. The Company and the Bank have no foreign assets or income.

At December 31, 2025, the Company had consolidated total assets of $4.4 billion, net loans of $3.0 billion, total deposits excluding brokered deposits of $3.5 billion and total shareholders' equity of $465.4 million. For the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company recognized consolidated net income of $28.2 million. The principal source of revenue for the Company and the Bank is interest and fees on loans. On a consolidated basis, interest and fees on loans accounted for 76%, 64%, and 60% of total revenues in 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively. Interest on securities accounted for 12%, 19%, and 24% of total revenues in 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively. For more information about the Company's financial condition and results of operations, see the consolidated financial statements and related notes included in Item 8 of this report.

There are a number of larger commercial banks and credit unions within the Bank's primary market areas. The Bank also competes with a large number of other financial institutions, such as savings and loan associations, insurance companies, consumer finance companies, internet banks and other financial technology companies, and commercial finance and leasing companies for deposits, loans and service business. Money market mutual funds, brokerage houses and nonfinancial institutions provide many of the financial services offered by the Bank. Many of these competitors have substantially greater resources than the Bank. The principal methods of competition for financial services are price (the rates of interest charged for loans, the rates of interest paid for deposits and the fees charged for services) and the convenience and quality of services rendered to customers.

Banks and bank holding companies are extensively regulated. The Company is subject to supervision and regulation by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (the "Federal Reserve Board"). The Company's activities are generally limited to owning or controlling banks and engaging in such other activities as the Federal Reserve Board may determine to be closely related to banking. Prior approval of the Federal Reserve Board, and in some cases various other government agencies, is required for the Company to

acquire control of any additional bank holding companies, banks or other operating subsidiaries. Under Federal Reserve Board policy, the Company is expected to act as a source of financial strength to the Bank and to commit resources to support it.

The Bank is chartered under state law and is subject to regulation by the Michigan Department of Insurance and Financial Services ("DIFS"). State banking laws place restrictions on various aspects of banking, including permitted activities, loan interest rates, branching, payment of dividends and capital and surplus requirements. The Bank is a member of the Federal Reserve System and is also subject to regulation by the Federal Reserve Board. The Bank's deposits are insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (the "FDIC") to the maximum extent provided by law. The Bank is a member of the Federal Home Loan Bank system, which provides certain advantages to the Bank, including favorable borrowing rates for certain funds.

The Company is a legal entity separate and distinct from the Bank. The Company's primary source of funds available to pay dividends to shareholders is dividends paid to it by the Bank. There are legal limitations on the extent to which the Bank can lend or otherwise supply funds to the Company. In addition, payment of dividends to the Company by the Bank is subject to various state and federal regulatory limitations.

As an FDIC-insured institution, the Bank is required to pay deposit insurance premium assessments to the FDIC. The FDIC has adopted a risk-based assessment system under which all insured depository institutions are placed into one of four categories and assessed insurance premiums, based upon their respective levels of capital and results of supervisory evaluation. Institutions categorized as well-capitalized (as defined by the FDIC) and considered healthy pay the lowest premium, while institutions that are categorized as less than adequately capitalized (as defined by the FDIC) and considered of substantial supervisory concern pay the highest premium. Risk classification of all insured institutions is made by the FDIC for each semi-annual assessment period.

The federal banking agencies have adopted guidelines to promote the safety and soundness of federally-insured depository institutions. These guidelines establish standards for, among other things, internal controls, information systems, internal audit systems, loan documentation, credit underwriting, interest rate exposure, asset growth, compensation, fees and benefits, asset quality and earnings.

The Company and the Bank are subject to regulatory "risk-based" capital guidelines. Failure to meet these capital guidelines could subject the Company or the Bank to a variety of enforcement remedies, including issuance of a capital directive, the termination of deposit insurance by the FDIC, a prohibition on accepting brokered deposits, and other restrictions on its business. In addition, the Bank would generally not receive regulatory approval of any application that requires the consideration of capital adequacy, such as a branch or merger application, unless it could demonstrate a reasonable plan to meet the capital requirement within a reasonable period of time.

Under Federal Reserve Board policy, the Company is expected to act as a source of financial strength to the Bank and to commit resources to support the Bank. In addition, if DIFS deems the Bank's capital to be impaired, DIFS may require the Bank to restore its capital by a special assessment on the Company as the Bank's sole shareholder. If the Company fails to pay any assessment, the Company's directors will be required, under Michigan law, to sell the shares of the Bank's stock owned by the Company to the highest bidder at either a public or private auction and use the proceeds of the sale to restore the Bank's capital.

The Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation Improvement Act ("FDICIA") requires, among other things, federal banking agencies to take "prompt corrective action" in respect of depository institutions that do not meet minimum capital requirements. FDICIA sets forth the following five capital categories: "well-capitalized," "adequately-capitalized," "undercapitalized," "significantly-undercapitalized" and "critically-undercapitalized." A depository institution's capital category will depend upon how its capital levels compare with various relevant capital measures as established by regulation, which include a common equity Tier I risk-based capital ratio, a Tier 1 risk-based capital ratio, a total risk-based capital ratio and a leverage capital ratio. In addition, a capital conservation buffer is required. Under certain circumstances, the appropriate banking agency may treat a well-capitalized, adequately-capitalized, or undercapitalized institution as if the institution were in the next lower capital category.

headings: Risks Related to the Company's Business
Asset quality could be less favorable than expected.
The Company's allowance for credit losses may not be adequate to cover actual credit losses.
General economic conditions in the state of Michigan could have a material adverse effect on the Company's results of operations or financial condition.
We may be adversely affected by risks associated with future mergers and acquisitions, including execution risk, which could disrupt our business and dilute shareholder value.
The Company could be adversely affected by the soundness of other financial institutions, including defaults by larger financial institutions.
If the Company does not adjust to changes in the financial services industry, its financial performance may suffer.
We are subject to significant government regulation, and any regulatory changes may adversely affect us.
Changes in interest rates could reduce the Company's income and cash flow.
The Company is subject to liquidity risk in its operations, which could adversely affect its ability to fund various obligations.

Evaluation of investment securities for an allowance for credit losses involves subjective determinations and could have a material adverse impact on our results of operations and financial condition.
The Company has significant exposure to risks associated with commercial and residential real estate.
Commercial loans may expose the Company to greater financial and credit risk than other loans.
Legislative or regulatory changes or actions could adversely impact the Company or the businesses in which it is engaged.
The Company relies heavily on its management and other key personnel, and the loss of any of them may adversely affect its operations.
The Company's controls and procedures may fail or be circumvented.
The Company may be a defendant in a variety of litigation and other actions, which may have a material adverse effect on the Company's financial condition and results of operations.
If the Company cannot raise additional capital when needed, its ability to further expand its operations through organic growth or acquisitions could be materially impaired.
Unauthorized disclosure of sensitive or confidential client or customer information, whether through a breach of computer systems or otherwise, could severely harm the Company's business.
The Company's information systems may experience an interruption or breach in security.
Cybersecurity incidents could disrupt business operations, result in the loss of critical and confidential information, and adversely impact our reputation and results of operations.
Employee misconduct could adversely impact our reputation and results of operations.
Environmental liability associated with commercial lending could result in losses.
The Company depends upon the accuracy and completeness of information about customers.
Our reliance on third party vendors could cause operational losses or business interruptions.
Severe weather, natural disasters, acts of war or terrorism, a public health crisis, and other external events could significantly impact the Company's business.
The Company relies on dividends from the Bank for most of its revenue.
Additional risks and uncertainties could have a negative effect on financial performance.
Risks Related to the Company's Common Stock
Investments in the Company's common stock involve risk.
The Company's common stock, while publicly traded, has less liquidity than the average liquidity of stocks listed on the Nasdaq Stock Market.
The Company's common stock is not insured by any government entity.
A shareholder's ownership of common stock may be diluted if the Company issues additional shares of common stock in the future.
The value of the Company's common stock may be adversely affected if the Company issues debt and equity securities that are senior to the Company's common stock in liquidation or as to distributions.
The Company's articles of incorporation and bylaws, and certain provisions of Michigan law, contain provisions that could make a takeover effort more difficult.
paragraphs: The Company is subject to many risks and uncertainties. Although the Company seeks ways to manage these risks and develop programs to control risks to the extent that management can control them, the Company cannot predict the future. Actual results may differ materially from management's expectations. Some of these significant risks and uncertainties are discussed below. The risks and uncertainties described below are not the only ones that the Company faces. Additional risks and uncertainties of which the Company is unaware, or that it currently does not consider to be material, also may become important factors that affect the Company and its business. If any of these risks were to occur, the Company's business, financial condition or results of operations could be materially and adversely affected.

A significant source of risk for the Company arises from the possibility that losses will be sustained because borrowers, guarantors and related parties may fail to perform in accordance with the terms of their loan agreements. Most loans originated by the Company are secured, but some loans are unsecured depending on the nature of the loan. With respect to secured loans, the collateral securing the repayment of these loans includes a wide variety of real and personal property that may be insufficient to cover the obligations owed under such loans. Collateral values may be adversely affected by changes in prevailing economic, environmental and other conditions, including declines in the value of real estate, changes in interest rates, changes in monetary and fiscal policies of the federal government, terrorist activity, environmental contamination, public health crisis, and other external events.

The risk of nonpayment of loans is inherent in all lending activities and nonpayment of loans may have a material adverse effect on the Company's earnings and overall financial condition, and the value of its common stock. The Company makes various assumptions and judgments about the collectability of its loan portfolio and provides an allowance for credit losses based on a number of factors. If its assumptions are wrong, the allowance for credit losses may not be sufficient to cover losses, which could have an adverse effect on the Company's operating results and may cause it to increase the allowance in the future. The actual amount of future provisions for credit losses cannot now be determined and may exceed the amounts of past provisions for credit losses. Federal and state banking regulators, as an integral part of their supervisory function, periodically review the allowance for credit losses. These regulatory agencies may require the Company to increase its allowance for credit losses or to recognize further loan charge-offs based upon their judgments, which may be different from the Company's judgments. Any increase in the allowance for credit losses could have a negative effect on the Company's regulatory capital ratios, net income, financial condition and results of operations.

The Company is affected by general economic conditions in the United States, although most directly within Michigan. An economic downturn within Michigan caused by inflation, recession or a recessionary environment, trade tariffs, trade policy or retaliatory measures by trade partners, unemployment, changes in financial or capital markets or other factors, could negatively impact household and corporate incomes. This impact may lead to decreased demand for both loan and deposit products and increase the number of customers who fail to pay interest or principal on their loans.

We plan to grow our business both organically and through mergers and acquisitions. We periodically evaluate merger and acquisition opportunities and conduct due diligence activities related to possible transactions with other financial institutions and financial services companies. As a result, we may engage in discussions or negotiations that, if they were to result in a transaction, could have a material effect on our operating results and financial condition. Our merger and acquisition activities could be material and could require us to use a substantial amount of common stock, preferred stock, cash, other liquid assets, and/or incur debt. Furthermore, failure to realize the expected revenue increases, cost savings, increases in geographic or product presence, and/or other projected benefits from our merger and acquisition activities could have a material adverse effect on our financial condition and results of operations.

The Company's ability to engage in routine funding transactions could be adversely affected by the actions and commercial soundness of other financial institutions. Financial services institutions are interrelated as a result of credit, trading, clearing, counterparty or other relationships between financial institutions. The Company has exposure to multiple counterparties, and it routinely executes transactions with counterparties in the financial industry. As a result, defaults by, or even rumors or questions about, one or more financial services institutions, or the financial services industry generally, could lead to market-wide liquidity problems and losses or defaults by the Company or by other institutions. This is sometimes referred to as "systemic risk" and may adversely affect financial intermediaries, such as clearing agencies, clearing houses, banks, securities firms and exchanges, with which the Company interacts on a daily basis, and therefore could adversely affect the Company.

paragraphs: ChoiceOne Financial Services, Inc. (the "Company") 為依 1956 年銀行控股公司法（"BHC Act"）註冊之金融控股公司。本公司於 1986 年 2 月 24 日成立為密歇根州公司。本公司成立之目的是建立銀行控股公司，以取得 ChoiceOne Bank 全部資本股票，該銀行於 1987 年 4 月 6 日成為本公司之 wholly owned subsidiary。自 2006 年 11 月 1 日起，Valley Ridge Financial Corp.（一家 Valley Ridge Bank（"VRB"）之單一銀行控股公司）與本公司合併。2006 年 12 月，VRB 被併入 ChoiceOne Bank。自 2019 年 10 月 1 日起，County Bank Corp.（"County"），一家 Lakestone Bank & Trust（"Lakestone"）之單一銀行控股公司，與本公司合併。Lakestone 於 2020 年 5 月被併入 ChoiceOne Bank。2020 年 7 月 1 日，Community Shores Bank Corporation（"Community Shores"），一家 Community Shores Bank 之單一銀行控股公司，與本公司合併。Community Shores Bank 於 2020 年 10 月被併入 ChoiceOne Bank。ChoiceOne Bank 持有 ChoiceOne Insurance Agencies, Inc. 全部已發行普通股，該獨立保險經紀公司總部設於密歇根州 Sparta（"Insurance Agency"）。2023 年 7 月 18 日，本公司成立 109 Technologies, LLC 為本公司之 wholly owned subsidiary，意圖擁有 fintech 產品之智慧財產權，該產品已授權予第三方銀行及銀行控股公司。2025 年 3 月 1 日，本公司完成 Fentura Financial, Inc.（"Fentura"），前 The State Bank 之母公司，與本公司合併，本公司為合併後之存續公司。2025 年 3 月 14 日，ChoiceOne Bank 完成 The State Bank 併入 ChoiceOne Bank，ChoiceOne Bank 為併入後之存續銀行。

本公司業務主要集中於單一產業分部，即銀行業。ChoiceOne Bank（簡稱 "Bank"）為一家提供多種存款、付款、信貸及其他金融服務之全方位銀行機構，服務所有類型之客戶。這些服務包括定期存款、儲蓄存款、活期存款、保管箱服務及自動交易機器服務。貸款，包括商業及消費貸款，主要以擔保方式提供給商業企業及個人。商業貸款涵蓋如企業、工業、農業、建設、存貨及不動產等類別。Bank 之消費貸款部門直接及間接向消費者及住宅及不動產購買新屋之買家提供貸款。此外，Bank 還提供信託及資產管理服務。本公司或 Bank 之業務並無依賴單一客戶或極少數客戶，若這些客戶流失，將不會對本公司造成重大不利影響。
Bank 之主要市場位於密歇根州西部、中部及東南部，為 Bank 之各辦公室所在地之社區。Bank 透過 47 間全方位辦公室、1 間 drive up 辦公室、5 間貸款業務辦公室及 1 間資產管理辦公室服務這些市場。本公司及 Bank 無任何海外資產或收入。

截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司合併總資產為 4.4 十億美元，合併總貸款為 3.0 十億美元，合併總存款（不含經紀存款）為 3.5 十億美元，合併總股東權益為 465.4 百萬美元。2025 年度，本公司合併總淨收入為 28.2 百萬美元。本公司及 Bank 之主要收入來源為貸款之利息及費用。合併基礎下，貸款之利息及費用在 2025 年、2024 年及 2023 年分別佔總收入之 76%、64% 及 60%。證券之利息在 2025 年、2024 年及 2023 年分別佔總收入之 12%、19% 及 24%。如需瞭解本公司財務狀況及營運成果之更多資訊，請參閱本報告第 8 項所附之合併財務報表及相關附註。

Bank 之主要市場區域內有許多大型商業銀行及信用合作社。Bank 亦與許多其他金融機構競爭，例如儲蓄貸款協會、保險公司、消費者金融公司、網際銀行及其他金融科技公司，以及商業金融及租賃公司，以爭取存款、貸款及服務業務。貨幣市場共同基金、證券經紀公司及非金融機構提供許多 Bank 所提供的金融服務。許多這些競爭對手擁有遠較 Bank 更多之資源。金融服務之主要競爭方式為價格（貸款之利率、存款之利率及服務費用）以及服務之便利性及品質。
銀行及銀行控股公司受到廣泛監管。本公司受美國聯邦儲備系統（"Federal Reserve Board"）之監督及管理。本公司之業務一般限於擁有或控制銀行，並從事聯邦儲備系統認為與銀行業務密切相關之其他活動。本公司欲
取得任何其他銀行控股公司、銀行或其他營運子公司之控制權，須經聯邦儲備系統之事先批准，某些情況下亦需經其他政府機構之批准。根據聯邦儲備系統政策，本公司被期望成為 Bank 之財務強大來源，並承諾資源支持 Bank。

Bank 為依州法律設立之銀行，受密歇根州保險及金融服務部門（"DIFS"）之監管。州銀行法對銀行之各項方面設有限制，包括允許之業務、貸款利率、分支機構設立、股息支付及資本與盈餘要求。Bank 為美國聯邦儲備系統之成員，亦受聯邦儲備系統之監管。Bank 之存款由美國存款保險公司（"FDIC"）根據法律規定之最高額度投保。Bank 為美國聯邦住宅貸款銀行系統之成員，該系統為 Bank 提供某些優勢，包括對某些資金之優惠借款利率。
本公司為一獨立法人的法律實體，與銀行為完全分離且獨立之實體。本公司用以支付股息予股東之主要資金來源為銀行所支付之股息。銀行對本公司提供貸款或其他資金之範圍存在法律限制。此外，銀行支付股息予本公司亦受各州及聯邦監管機構之限制。

作為美國聯邦存款保險公司（FDIC）所 insure 之機構，該銀行須支付存款保險費予 FDIC。FDIC 已採用基於風險之評估制度，將所有受保存款機構歸類為四個等級之一，並根據其資本水準及監管評估結果收取保險費。被歸類為資本充足（依 FDIC 所定義）且被視為健康的機構，支付最低保險費；而被歸類為資本不足（依 FDIC 所定義）且被視為監管關注之機構，則支付最高保險費。所有受保機構之風險分類由 FDIC 針對每半年度評估期間進行。
美國聯邦銀行監管機構已制定指南，以促進受聯邦保險之存款機構之安全與健全。這些指南設定了標準，包括但不限於內部控制、資訊系統、內部稽核系統、貸款文件、信貸評估、利率風險、資產成長、薪酬、費用與福利、資產品質及營收等。
本公司與銀行均受「基於風險」資本指南之規範。未能符合這些資本指南，可能使本公司或銀行面臨多種處罰措施，包括發出資本指令、FDIC 中止存款保險、禁止接受經紀存款，及其他對其業務之限制。此外，銀行通常不會獲得任何需考量資本充足性之申請之監管批准，例如分行或合併申請，除非其能證明在合理期間內有合理計畫以符合資本要求。
根據美國聯邦儲備銀行政策，本公司被期望作為銀行之財務強化來源，並承諾資源以支援銀行。此外，若密歇根州存款保險基金（DIFS）認為銀行之資本受損，DIFS 可要求銀行透過對本公司之特別評估，以恢復其資本。若本公司未能支付任何評估費用，根據密歇根州法律，本公司董事會將被要求出售本公司所持有之銀行股票予最高出價者，透過公開或私下拍賣，並以拍賣所得金額恢復銀行之資本。

根據《美國聯邦存款保險公司改善法案》（FDICIA），美國聯邦銀行監管機構須對未達最低資本要求之存款機構採取「即時修正措施」。FDICIA 規定以下五種資本分級：「資本充足」、「資本足夠」、「資本不足」、「嚴重資本不足」及「極度資本不足」。存款機構之資本分級將根據其資本水準與各項相關資本指標之比較而定，這些指標包括常見權益一級風險資本比率、一級風險資本比率、總風險資本比率及槓桿資本比率。此外，亦需符合資本儲備緩衝要求。在某些情況下，適當之銀行監管機構可將資本充足、資本足夠或資本不足之機構視為處於下一個較低資本分級。

headings: 與本公司業務相關的風險
本公司資產品質可能不如預期優良。
本公司對於信用損失的撥備可能不足以涵蓋實際發生的信用損失。
密歇根州總體經濟狀況可能對本公司營運成果或財務狀況造成重大不利影響。
本公司可能因未來合併與收購相關風險而受到不利影響，包括執行風險，此等風險可能幹擾本公司營運並稀釋股東價值。
本公司可能因其他金融機構的營運狀況而受到不利影響，包括較大規模金融機構的違約。
若本公司未能適應金融服務業的變革，其財務表現可能受影響。
本公司受重大政府監管，任何監管變更可能對本公司造成不利影響。
利率變動可能降低本公司的營業收入與現金流。
本公司在營運中面臨流動性風險，可能不利於其履行各項義務的能力。
評估投資證券之信用減損撥備涉及主觀判斷，可能對我們之營運成果與財務狀況造成重大不利影響。
本公司對商業及住宅不動產相關風險有重大曝險。
商業貸款可能使本公司面臨較其他貸款更高的財務與信用風險。
立法或監管變動或措施可能對本公司或其從事之業務造成不利影響。
本公司高度依賴其管理階層及其他關鍵人員，任何其人之流失可能不利於本公司營運。
本公司之內控與程序可能失效或遭繞過。
本公司可能成為多種訴訟及其他行動的被告，這可能會對本公司的財務狀況及營運成果產生重大不利影響。
若本公司無法在需要時籌措額外資金，其透過內生成長或收購進一步擴展營運能力的能力可能會受到重大影響。
未經授權揭露敏感或機密的客戶資訊，無論是透過電腦系統遭入侵或其他方式，都可能嚴重損害本公司的業務。
本公司的資訊系統可能遭遇中斷或安全漏洞。
網路安全事件可能幹擾營運，導致關鍵且機密資訊遺失，並對本公司聲譽及營運成果產生負面影響。
員工不當行為可能對本公司聲譽及營運成果產生負面影響。
與商業貸款相關的環境責任可能會導致損失。
本公司依賴有關客戶資訊的準確性與完整性。
本公司對第三方廠商之依賴可能導致營運損失或業務中斷。
極端天氣、天然災害、戰爭行為或恐怖攻擊、公共衛生危機及其他外部事件，可能對本公司業務產生重大影響。
本公司大部分收入來自銀行所發放之股息。
其他風險與不確定因素可能對財務表現產生負面影響。
與本公司普通股相關之風險
投資本公司普通股涉及風險。
本公司普通股雖為公開交易股票，但其流動性低於納斯達克股票市場上市股票之平均流動性。
本公司普通股未經任何政府機構投保。
股東持有普通股之權益可能因本公司未來發行更多普通股而遭稀釋。
若本公司發行之債務及權益證券優先於本公司普通股於清算或分派時受償，則本公司普通股之價值可能受不利影響。
本公司章程及章程細則，以及密歇根州法律之特定條款，包含可能使收購行動更困難之規定。
paragraphs: 本公司面臨許多風險與不確定性。雖然本公司尋求方法來管理這些風險並發展方案以控制風險，至管理層所能控制的程度，本公司無法預測未來。實際結果可能與管理層的預期有重大差異。其中一些重要的風險與不確定性於下文討論。下列所描述的風險與不確定性並非本公司所面臨的唯一風險。此外，本公司可能未察覺或目前認為不具重大影響的其他風險與不確定性，也可能成為影響本公司及其業務的重要因素。如果其中任何風險發生，將可能對本公司的業務、財務狀況或營運成果造成重大且不利的影響。

對本公司而言，一個重要的風險來源是借款人、擔保人及相關方可能未能依照貸款協議的條款履行義務，導致產生損失。本公司所發放的貸款中，大多數為有擔保貸款，但根據貸款性質，部分貸款為無擔保貸款。針對有擔保貸款，用以償還貸款的擔保品包括種類繁多的實物與動產，這些擔保品可能不足以覆蓋貸款義務。擔保品價值可能因經濟、環境及其他條件的變化而受到不利影響，包括房地產價值下降、利率變動、聯邦政府貨幣與財政政策的變化、恐怖活動、環境污染、公共衛生危機及其他外部事件。

貸款無法償付的風險是所有貸款業務的內在風險，貸款無法償付可能對本公司的獲利與整體財務狀況造成重大不利影響，並影響其普通股價值。本公司會根據多種因素對貸款組合的回收可能性做出假設與判斷，並根據這些因素提供信用損失撥備。如果其假設錯誤，信用損失撥備可能不足以覆蓋實際損失，這可能會對本公司的營運成果造成不利影響，並可能導致本公司未來增加撥備。未來實際的信用損失撥備金額目前無法確定，可能高於過去的撥備金額。聯邦與州級銀行監管機構作為其監督功能的一部分，會定期審查信用損失撥備。這些監管機構可能要求本公司增加信用損失撥備或根據其判斷認列進一步的貸款減損，而這些判斷可能與本公司的判斷不同。信用損失撥備金額的增加可能對本公司的監管資本比率、淨收入、財務狀況與營運成果產生負面影響。
本公司受美國整體經濟狀況影響，雖然最直接的是密歇根州。密歇根州因通貨膨脹、經濟衰退或衰退環境、貿易關稅、貿易政策或貿易夥伴的報復措施、失業率、金融或資本市場的變化或其他因素所導致的經濟衰退，可能對家庭與企業收入造成負面影響。這種影響可能導致貸款與存款產品的需求減少，並增加未能償還貸款利息或本金的客戶數量。

我們計畫透過內生成長與併購來擴張業務。我們會定期評估併購機會，並進行與其他金融機構與金融服務公司的可能交易相關的盡職調查活動。因此，我們可能參與討論或談判，如果這些談判導致交易成功，可能會對我們的營運成果與財務狀況產生重大影響。我們的併購活動可能具有重大影響，並可能要求我們使用大量普通股、優先股、現金、其他流動資產，以及/或增加債務。此外，未能實現預期的收入增加、成本節省、地理或產品版圖的擴張，以及/或其他預期的併購效益，可能會對我們的財務狀況與營運成果造成重大不利影響。

本公司進行常規資金交易的能力可能受到其他金融機構行動與商業健全性影響。金融服務機構因信用、交易、清算、交易對手或其他關係而相互關聯。本公司對多個交易對手有敞口，並會與金融業的交易對手進行常規交易。因此，一個或幾個金融服務機構或金融服務業的違約、甚至只是 rumours 或疑慮，都可能導致市場流動性問題，並導致本公司或其他機構的損失或違約。這種情況有時被稱為 "系統性風險"，可能對本公司日常互動的清算機構、清算所、銀行、證券公司與交易所等金融中介機構造成不利影響，因此可能對本公司造成不利影響。
